messages:
Maria (IAM): Heads-up: hit a permission hole when testing moving project buckets up to org-level storage. A project-scoped API key was still able to read another project's mailbox via the service proxy. Not a full exploit but surprising. Anyone seen this pattern before?
Jake (runtime): Can you paste the minimal repro? sounds like a token-audience / principal mismatch.
Maria (IAM): Minimal repro: request has x-api-key for project:proj-17, proxy forwards as service principal svc-mailer and we rely on proxy headers to resolve project. Snip: 
```
GET /mailbox/proj-42/messages
Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>
X-Forwarded-Project: proj-17
X-Api-Key-Id: key-123
```
Proxy accepts X-Forwarded-Project and lets svc-mailer act on behalf of proj-17, but timesteps show svc-mailer still can access proj-42 mailbox because backend chooses service principal over forwarded project claim.
Sam (proxy): That matches something I saw in staging last week. Our principal resolution order is: explicit service principal > forwarded project > api-key-owner. We did this to avoid accidental privilege escalation when downstream lacks claim checks.
RBAC Bot: FYI role resolution policy currently documented as: service_takes_precedence=true. See /docs/authz/role-resolution.md.
Jake (runtime): Two ways to fix: (A) tighten backend to prefer requester (api-key owner) over service when X-Forwarded-Project present, or (B) require the proxy to inject a signed project claim (aud=backend) so backend can verify it wasn't spoofed. Option B is stronger but larger rollout.
Maria (IAM): Preference: B for long-term (signed assertion), but we need a compatibility path. Many customers have keys that assume old behavior.
Sam (proxy): Implementation sketch: proxy signs a small JWT with iss=redwood-proxy, aud=service-backend, sub=proj-17, exp=+5s, and forwards in X-Proxy-Assertion. Backend verifies signature against proxy's cert and enforces that jwt.sub == requested-project. Can do canary for a subset of tenants.
Jake (runtime): +1. Also add server-side fallback check: if no X-Proxy-Assertion, fall back to previous resolution but log and emit an audit event and rate-limit.
DevOps (oncall): Operational concerns: we'll need KMS rotation plan for proxy signing key and a way to revoke compromised assertions quickly. Also consider metrics: authz_failure_count, assertion_missing_count, assertion_verify_time.
Maria (IAM): Migration plan proposal: 1) Proxy implements signed assertion (Sam) and deploy to staging. 2) Runtime adds verification and logging fallback (Jake). 3) Run a week in permissive mode (verify only + alerts) and run audit script to list keys that rely on old flow (Maria). 4) Notify customers and flip to enforce.
Sam (proxy): I'll open a PR for the proxy signer and a small acceptance test for JWT verification. Can canary with internal orgs first.
Jake (runtime): I'll add permissive verification: verify if present, enforce only in enforce-mode flag. Will add an audit endpoint to list requests that used forwarded headers without valid assertion.
Maria (IAM): I'll prepare an inventory of project-scoped keys and owners so we can contact them during the canary.
RBAC Bot: Logging/telemetry checklist: capture header_present, assertion_valid, resolved_principal, resolved_roles.
DevOps (oncall): +1 on metrics and rotation. Also remind that sess tokens for internal services need a migration path: we'll need to issue short-lived proxy-signed assertions for those flows too.
Maria (IAM): Ok next steps: Sam prototype, Jake runtime permissive mode, Maria audit. If we hit no major issues in canary after 7 days we schedule enforcement. @Sam @Jake @DevOps please ack.
Sam (proxy): Ack :thumbsup:
Jake (runtime): Ack
DevOps (oncall): Ack
Maria (IAM): Thanks folks — filing follow-up RFC with links to PRs and rollout timeline.
